chief_complaint: Elevated blood pressure (stage 2 hypertension) with associated obesity and recent psychosocial stressors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 41-year-old man with a history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2021, currently uncontrolled (BP 135/103 mmHg, diastolic ≥100). Obesity was documented in October 2024 (BMI ≥30). He has longstanding prediabetes (A1c 6.3% since 2009) and chronic anemia. Pulmonic valve regurgitation has been present since 1990 without recent cardiac imaging. Chronic sinusitis dates back to 1997, with an acute bacterial sinusitis episode resolved in October 2024. Since October 2024 he reports new stress and intimate‑partner abuse, while maintaining full‑time employment. No other antihypertensive agents or metabolic medications have been added, and laboratory data (eGFR, lipid panel) are missing.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple sprains (most recent 2025-01-21), prior part‑time employment (2022), several episodes of viral sinusitis (2020), an acute bacterial sinusitis resolved in October 2024, a tooth infection resolved in 2021, and medication review reminders that have been addressed. No chronic diseases beyond those listed as active have been documented as resolved.
social_determinants: White, non‑Hispanic male, residing in New Bedford, MA. Currently employed full‑time. Recent intimate‑partner abuse and high stress levels. High school education. No documented substance use or housing instability.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 2 hypertension (DBP 103), obesity (BMI ≥30), pulmonic valve regurgitation, elevated heart rate (98 bpm), and psychosocial stressors (intimate partner abuse, high stress). Metabolic risk: prediabetes (A1c 6.3%) and obesity. Hematologic risk: chronic anemia. Respiratory risk: chronic sinusitis. Renal risk: hypertension present but eGFR and albuminuria data missing. Mental health risk: stress and intimate‑partner violence. Overall Charlson comorbidity index 1, clinical complexity moderate.
